#!/bin/bash
# Installed by build-fleet/mini-ops/ops/console-unlock-guard.sh. Tested by
# build-fleet/mini-ops/console_unlock_guard_test.py, which runs this body with stub commands; keep
# every tool call a bare name (no /usr/bin prefixes) and every path overridable, as below.
set -u
dir=${CMUX_FLEET_OPS_DIR:-/Library/Application Support/cmux-fleet-ops}
fleet=${CMUX_FLEET_DIR:-/Users/Shared/cmux-build-fleet}
pref=${CMUX_LOGINWINDOW_PREF:-/Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow}
locked_checks=${CMUX_GUARD_LOCKED_CHECKS:-3}
restart_gap_s=${CMUX_GUARD_RESTART_GAP_S:-21600}   # 6 h: one guard restart per mini, then alert
fresh_boot_s=${CMUX_GUARD_FRESH_BOOT_S:-3600}
state="$dir/console-unlock-guard.locked"
restarts="$dir/console-unlock-guard.restarts"
alert="$dir/console-unlock-guard.alert"
say() { echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*"; }
# Every refusal a person has to clear goes through hold: the log line alone is read by nobody.
hold() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >"$alert" 2>/dev/null; say "$*"; exit 0; }
mkdir -p "$dir"   # a missing state dir must not silently lose the locked-check count

# --- keep the console from locking in the first place ----------------------------------------
if defaults read "$pref" autoLoginUserScreenLocked >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  defaults delete "$pref" autoLoginUserScreenLocked && say "autoLoginUserScreenLocked deleted"
fi
ds=$(pmset -g | awk '$1 == "displaysleep" {print $2}')
if [ -n "$ds" ] && [ "$ds" != 0 ]; then pmset -a displaysleep 0 && say "displaysleep $ds -> 0"; fi
# The screen saver is what locks an idle mini: loginwindow's default idle is 1200 s and the lock
# delay is 0. idleTime is a per-user ByHost pref, so it is written as the console user, in their
# session, not as root.
cuser=$(stat -f %Su /dev/console 2>/dev/null)
cuid=$(stat -f %u /dev/console 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$cuser" ] && [ "$cuser" != root ] && [ -n "$cuid" ]; then
  as_console() { launchctl asuser "$cuid" sudo -u "$cuser" "$@"; }
  idle=$(as_console defaults -currentHost read com.apple.screensaver idleTime 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "${idle:-unset}" != 0 ]; then
    as_console defaults -currentHost write com.apple.screensaver idleTime -int 0 \
      && say "screen saver idleTime ${idle:-default} -> 0 for $cuser"
  fi

  # Sound is per-user on macOS. Read first so every pass reports drift, then
  # repair it in the logged-in user's Aqua session. A missing session is a
  # reportable baseline gap; the next RunAtLoad/interval pass retries it.
  audio=$(as_console osascript \
    -e 'set s to get volume settings' \
    -e 'return (output muted of s as text) & "|" & (alert volume of s as text)' 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$audio" in
    true\|0) ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$audio" ]; then
        say "muted drift for $cuser: output/alert=$audio; repairing"
      else
        say "muted drift for $cuser: output/alert unreadable; repairing"
      fi
      as_console osascript \
        -e 'set volume output muted true' \
        -e 'set volume alert volume 0' \
        || say "muted drift for $cuser: osascript repair failed"
      ;;
  esac
  beep=$(as_console defaults read -g com.apple.sound.beep.volume 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$beep" in
    0|0.0) ;;
    *)
      say "muted drift for $cuser: com.apple.sound.beep.volume=${beep:-unreadable}; repairing"
      as_console defaults write -g com.apple.sound.beep.volume -float 0 \
        || say "muted drift for $cuser: beep preference repair failed"
      ;;
  esac
  uiaudio=$(as_console defaults read -g com.apple.sound.uiaudio.enabled 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$uiaudio" in
    0|false) ;;
    *)
      say "muted drift for $cuser: com.apple.sound.uiaudio.enabled=${uiaudio:-unreadable}; repairing"
      as_console defaults write -g com.apple.sound.uiaudio.enabled -bool false \
        || say "muted drift for $cuser: UI-audio preference repair failed"
      ;;
  esac
else
  say "muted drift: no non-root console user; waiting for Aqua session"
fi
# A restart must not be heard across the room.
if [ "$(nvram StartupMute 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}')" != "%01" ]; then
  nvram StartupMute=%01 && say "StartupMute -> %01 (silent startup)"
fi

# --- is the console locked? ------------------------------------------------------------------
users=$(ioreg -n Root -d1 -a | plutil -extract IOConsoleUsers json -o - - 2>/dev/null)
case "$users" in
  *'"CGSSessionScreenIsLocked":true'*) ;;
  *)
    if [ -f "$alert" ]; then say "console unlocked again; clearing the alert"; fi
    rm -f "$state" "$alert"; exit 0 ;;
esac
# A counter the guard cannot read must not stop it from ever counting again: $(( abc + 1 )) under
# set -u kills the run before it can overwrite the file, so the digits are what count.
count=$(cat "$state" 2>/dev/null)
count=${count//[!0-9]/}
n=$(( ${count:-0} + 1 ))
echo "$n" >"$state"
[ "$n" -ge "$locked_checks" ] || { say "console locked ($n/$locked_checks)"; exit 0; }

# --- FileVault: a restart would stop at the unlock screen ------------------------------------
# With FileVault on there is no auto-login after a restart: the mini waits at the FileVault unlock
# screen, off the network, until a person types a password. So the guard
# restarts only a mini fdesetup says is Off; On, or an answer it cannot read, holds for a person.
case "$(fdesetup status 2>/dev/null)" in
  *"FileVault is Off"*) ;;
  *) hold "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: FileVault is on (or fdesetup did not answer), so a restart would stop at its unlock screen until a person types a password. A person has to unlock this console." ;;
esac

# --- would a restart cost anyone work? -------------------------------------------------------
# Both helpers below fail closed: a python3 that cannot run reads as busy, never as free. Rebooting a
# mini out from under a reservation or a build is far worse than leaving a locked console locked.
busy=""
pgrep -f 'bin/Runner.Worker' >/dev/null && busy="a GitHub job"
pgrep -x xcodebuild >/dev/null && busy="xcodebuild"
pgrep -x xctest >/dev/null && busy="xctest"
if [ -z "$busy" ] && [ -e "$fleet/host.lock" ]; then
  /usr/bin/python3 - "$fleet/host.lock" <<'PY'
import fcntl, sys
# 0: the lock is free. 3: a build holds it. Anything else is an error, and an error means busy.
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    try:
        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
    except OSError:
        sys.exit(3)
PY
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" = 3 ]; then busy="host.lock"
  elif [ "$rc" != 0 ]; then busy="host.lock (could not read it: python3 exited $rc)"; fi
fi
if [ -z "$busy" ] && [ -f "$fleet/reservation.json" ]; then
  /usr/bin/python3 - "$fleet/reservation.json" <<'PY'
import json, sys, time
# Like the runner hook (glaeda_reservation.py): live when now < until. 3: the reservation expired, so
# the mini is free. 0: it is live. An unreadable or invalid file counts as reserved, and so does any
# other exit, including a python3 that is not there at all.
try:
    until = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("until")
except Exception:
    sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(3 if isinstance(until, int) and not isinstance(until, bool) and until <= time.time() else 0)
PY
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" = 0 ]; then busy="a reservation"
  elif [ "$rc" != 3 ]; then busy="a reservation (could not read it: python3 exited $rc)"; fi
fi
now=$(date +%s)
# kern.boottime reads "{ sec = 1792554887, usec = 684295 } Tue Oct 20 20:54:47 2026". A greedy
# ".*sec = " takes the usec, which made every uptime look like decades and the fresh-boot brake
# never hold, so minis rebooted every ~30 min. Field 4 is the seconds,
# and a boot time this cannot read refuses the restart instead of allowing it.
boot=$(sysctl -n kern.boottime 2>/dev/null | awk -F'[ ,]+' '{print $4}')
case "${boot:-}" in
  '' | *[!0-9]*) [ -z "$busy" ] && busy="kern.boottime unreadable" ;;
  *) [ -z "$busy" ] && [ "$(( now - boot ))" -lt "$fresh_boot_s" ] && busy="a restart under an hour ago" ;;
esac
if [ -n "$busy" ]; then
  # A busy check that could not run leaves the guard unable to heal anything, which is a state
  # somebody has to clear; an honestly busy mini is not.
  case "$busy" in
    *"could not read it"* | *unreadable*) hold "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: $busy" ;;
  esac
  say "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: $busy"
  exit 0
fi

# --- one restart per 6 h, then alert instead -------------------------------------------------
# $restarts is the whole bound, and it has to survive the reboot it is bounding. So a history this
# cannot read, and a restart it cannot write down, both refuse the restart: a mini whose disk is full
# would otherwise reboot every 10 minutes, which is the loop this guard exists to end.
last=""
if [ -d "$restarts" ]; then
  hold "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: cannot read $restarts, so the 6 h bound is unknown"
fi
if [ -e "$restarts" ] && ! last=$(tail -1 "$restarts" 2>/dev/null); then
  hold "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: cannot read $restarts, so the 6 h bound is unknown"
fi
case "$last" in
  '') ;;
  *[!0-9]*) hold "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: $restarts holds something that is not a timestamp" ;;
esac
# An epoch is exactly 10 digits from 2001 to 2286. More means two lines ran together (a truncated
# write), and arithmetic on 20 digits overflows silently into a number that passes any bound; fewer
# means a truncated epoch, which reads as a restart in 1970 and would allow one more reboot.
if [ -n "$last" ] && [ "${#last}" != 10 ]; then
  hold "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: $restarts holds an implausible timestamp (${#last} digits)"
fi
if [ -n "$last" ] && [ "$last" -gt "$now" ]; then
  hold "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: $restarts says the last restart is in the future"
fi
if [ -n "$last" ] && [ "$(( now - last ))" -lt "$restart_gap_s" ]; then
  hold "restarted $(( (now - last) / 60 ))m ago and the console is locked again: not restarting again for $(( restart_gap_s / 3600 ))h. A person has to look at this mini (auto-login is coming back locked)."
fi
# Every restart the guard makes, newest last. The bare echo guarantees a line break, so a history
# that lost its trailing newline cannot glue two epochs into one number.
{ cat "$restarts" 2>/dev/null; echo; echo "$now"; } | grep -E '^[0-9]{10}$' | tail -20 >"$restarts.next" 2>/dev/null
mv -f "$restarts.next" "$restarts" 2>/dev/null
chmod 644 "$restarts" 2>/dev/null
if [ "$(tail -1 "$restarts" 2>/dev/null)" != "$now" ]; then
  rm -f "$restarts.next"
  hold "console locked ($n checks); not restarting: could not record this restart in $restarts, so the 6 h bound would not survive the reboot"
fi
rm -f "$state" "$alert"
say "console locked for $n checks and the mini is idle: restarting so auto-login starts unlocked"
shutdown -r now

symbol-cache-cap.body:
#!/bin/bash
# Installed by build-fleet/mini-ops/ops/symbol-cache-cap.sh.
f=/System/Volumes/Data/System/Library/Caches/com.apple.coresymbolicationd/data
[ -f "$f" ] || exit 0
size=$(stat -f %z "$f")
(( size > 20 * 1000000000 )) || exit 0
rm -f "$f"
launchctl kickstart -k system/com.apple.coresymbolicationd
echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) removed $((size / 1000000000)) GB symbolication cache"
